title: WestJet first told Boeing about 737 MAX software glitch cleared by FAA, memo says
excerpt: WestJet pilots were conducting an ​entry-into-service validation flight with ‌a Boeing 737 MAX in 2024, ​when they uncovered ​an anomaly linked to ⁠the jet's flight ​computer software that ​was deemed safe by the Federal Aviation Administration ​on Friday.
content_html:
By Reuters

October 2, 20267:50 PM UTCUpdated ago

  • Companies

Oct 2 (Reuters) - WestJet pilots were conducting an ​entry-into-service validation flight with ‌a Boeing

(BA.N), opens new tab

737 MAX in 2024, ​when they uncovered ​an anomaly linked to ⁠the jet's flight ​computer software that ​was deemed safe by the Federal Aviation Administration ​on Friday.

The Canadian ​carrier was the first to ‌report ⁠the anomaly to Boeing with supporting data, according to ​the ​memo ⁠to pilots on Friday seen ​by Reuters, ​after ⁠the FAA concluded a Corrective Action Review ⁠Board ​on the ​issue.
